gate_selection.rationale: G0 is PASS; G1 is the lowest FAIL gate with satisfied dependency — coverage is the next question to answer.

impl_result.notes: Fix applied: deps_adj.footprint() now includes visit_mask tiles (bit SET = visitable approach tile) alongside the existing blocked tiles + anchor. This recovers the mine→guard coupling that the strict immediate-touch graph dropped — guard entries now appear in mine profiles (e.g., grass|mine: randomMonsterLevel2 share=0.026). Zero-weights check: the shuffled control (same types, random positions) scores 3.51 vs the graph's 3.25, confirming the graph adds genuine structure. The fix improved the control margin from ~0.12 (pre-fix smoke) to 0.26 at gate scale. Gate is still FAIL: mean_objdist 3.25 > 2.5 threshold and only 50% of maps within 3.0 tiles. The hardest-to-fit maps (The Five Rings 4.6, A Viking We Shall Go Allied 4.39, Search for the Grail 4.39) appear to be complex multi-player maps where the generator's graph structure diverges most from the real layout. All 19 tests pass (10 G0 + 9 G1); ruff format + check clean.

gate_check.notes: All four G0 criteria satisfied. (1) benchmark.py --maps 8 --seeds 4 exits 0, runtime ~90s. (2) Output JSON contains coverage.mean_control_objdist and reconstruct.control_objdist alongside all three scores. (3) Two back-to-back runs produced identical output: mean_objdist 3.66, pass_rate 0.0 — fully deterministic. (4) _shuffled_objdist() iterates fm['objects'] from the best-fit generated map (best[5]) and reassigns positions to random free tiles — same object multiset, fair within-map control. pytest 10/10 passed. No special-casing of any map found in benchmark.py, deps_fit.py, or deps_realize.py. reachability_repair is a physical path-carving routine (removes decoration/mountains only, never gameplay objects) — not a metric-gaming shortcut; notably, validity pass_rate is 0.0 even with it, confirming it does not inflate the score. Advance to G1.
